hypothesis: Raising EasyCache's native transform-distance threshold to 0.20 with a two-hit cap, calibrated from round-2 traces, will produce approximately 28 hits and approach the aggressive 28.0-28.5 second TeaCache/TaylorSeer band while revealing the family's matched-budget quality behavior.

build.tests: 9/9 CPU tests passed; EasyCache calibration/hit behavior, ledger validation, dry-run, git diff, exact lease UUID, GPU-idle, and shared-lock availability preflights passed. The optional DeepGEMM warning remained benign.

run.signal_definition: EasyCache runtime-adaptive input-to-output transformation rate multiplied by current token-subsampled input change and normalized by previous output magnitude
run.reuse_payload: separate conditional and unconditional full-block-stack residual histories

validity.visual_note: The first/middle/last frames remain coherent and visibly much closer to dense than aggressive TeaCache round 3 and especially TaylorSeer round 4. Identity, anatomy, forest/tree placement, and flare progression remain near baseline; low-to-moderate endpoint framing, gaze, and flare drift is visible, but there is no gross anatomy or progression artifact.

decision.reason: Retain as a strongly informative aggressive EasyCache calibration/frontier point: the source-calibrated 28-hit prediction was exact, the method and artifact are valid, 29.2 s provides a 2.113x speedup, and the independent lightweight screen makes it the provisional aggressive quality leader. It is 2.456% slower than TeaCache round 3, so it is not yet the official matched aggressive comparator.
